methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 18.9x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Ranovus is a Series D+ stage semiconductor company that has raised $236M including a $36M strategic investment fund grant in August 2025. The target operates within a fragmented Chips & Semiconductors sector comprising 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, Etched, and Ayar Labs.

Triangulation analysis was limited by data constraints. Peer-median valuation could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow semiconductor peer set; while 13 companies operate in the sector, filtering by stage and valuation tier yielded fewer than the 3 minimum datapoints required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring proved inapplicable because Ranovus's revenue—typical proprietary information for private companies—was not available. The median public semiconductor P/S multiple is 18.9x across the three public tickers, but without disclosed revenue this multiple cannot be operationalized.

The analysis cannot support a specific valuation range given these methodological constraints. Ranovus's $236M total capital raised provides a floor reference point, but does not establish enterprise value. Practitioners seeking valuation clarity would require either: (1) Ranovus revenue disclosure enabling public-comp P/S anchoring, or (2) access to contemporaneous pricing data from comparable Series D+ semiconductor raises. Stage, funding velocity, and the strategic nature of the SIF grant suggest material value, but quantitative support remains absent.
